report_name: Brown Health Medical Group Breach Exposes Data of 311,000 People

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Attacker
threat_actors.description: The unauthorized party responsible for the data breach at Brown Health Medical Group-MA by accessing a legacy file server in December 2025.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The attacker accessed a large volume of unstructured sensitive data, including PII, PHI, and financial information, stored on a compromised legacy file server.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The attacker exfiltrated sensitive personal, financial, and protected health information from the compromised legacy file server.

identities.name: Brown Health Medical Group-MA
identities.description: A healthcare provider operated by Lifespan Physician Group that suffered a data breach affecting 311,760 individuals after an attacker accessed a legacy file server.

identities.name: Lifespan Physician Group of Massachusetts, Inc.
identities.description: The operator of Brown Health Medical Group-MA, which reported the data breach.

identities.name: Hawthorn Medical Associates
identities.description: The physical location where the compromised legacy file server was located.

indicators.name: Anomalous File Share Access Indicative of Data Staging
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous File Share Access Indicative of Data Staging
id: 2b1a9c8d-4e5f-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a high number of file/folder access events (Event ID 4663) from a single source, potentially indicating reconnaissance or data staging from a file server, as seen in the Brown Health Medical Group breach. This rule is a baseline and should be tuned with appropriate thresholds in a SIEM.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/311000-impacted-by-brown-health-medical-group-ma-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1005
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4663
    ObjectType: 'File'
    AccessList|contains:
      - '%%4416' # ReadData
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects anomalous access patterns to file servers, such as a high volume of file reads from a single account, which could indicate data staging or exfiltration activity.

indicators.name: Suspicious Logon to Legacy Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Logon to Legacy Server
id: 8c9d0e1f-2a3b-4c5d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects logon events (Event ID 4624) to servers that may be considered unusual. This could indicate compromised credentials being used, as potentially occurred in the Brown Health Medical Group breach. This rule should be customized to filter for legacy servers and exclude known service accounts.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/311000-impacted-by-brown-health-medical-group-ma-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.lateral_movement
level: low
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3 # Network Logon
  filter_known_accounts:
    AccountName|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_accounts
indicators.description: Detects logon events to servers that may be considered unusual, such as outside business hours or from non-standard accounts, which could indicate compromised credential usage.

relationships.target_name: Lifespan Physician Group of Massachusetts, Inc.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous File Share Access Indicative of Data Staging
